chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Forming a cooperative band after Isham Jones retired in 1936
summary: When Jones retired, five members set up a stockholder corporation modelled on Bob Crosby's band. It ran as a cooperative for eight or nine years before dissolving.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And so, when Isham decided to retire in 1936, early

in '36, that's when we had a couple of meetings, the guys in the Isham Jones band and myself. And about five of us eventually stuck together, with the intent of doing what the Bob Crosby band had done, which originally had been the Pollock band, and that was to set up a corporation, and each member, at least of the original grouping, would be stockholders. And then we would hire the musicians and work as a going unit. And so that's how the first band started, and I was more or less -- there was never any serious discussion about who would stand in front of the band or anything, because I guess I was expected to, and that's the way it turned out.

And for the first few years, we operated as a -- quite a few years, about eight or nine years, we operated as a cooperative band. The only problem with that, I found, as the guy who stands in front of it, you have to have board meetings if you want to go to the men's room, and this gets to be a pretty heavy thing.
So I decided then that if there was ever going to be a change, it would be to just have one leader and one person to operate the thing. How the money would get distributed was something else.
It was dissolved, because eventually, during the way, almost everyone who was originally with me was drafted out, or they left of their own accord, because the
going was very rough, and so then I wound up with the thing.
